record.title: Hansen–Vukicevic's conjecture for commuting and non-commuting graphs of finite groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian group, and let $\Gamma(G)$ denote either the commuting graph or the non-commuting graph of $G$. Its first and second Zagreb indices are

$$
M_{1}(\Gamma(G))=\sum_{v\in v(\Gamma(G))}\deg(v)^2,\qquad M_{2}(\Gamma(G))=\sum_{uv\in e(\Gamma(G))}\deg(u)\deg(v).
$$

**Hansen–Vuki\v{c}evi\'{c}'s conjecture for group graphs.**

$$
\frac{M_{2}(\Gamma(G))}{|e(\Gamma(G))|}\geq\frac{M_{1}(\Gamma(G))}{|v(\Gamma(G))|}.
$$

The authors report computational verification for commuting and non-commuting graphs of finite non-abelian groups of order at most $1000$. The conjecture remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Complete permutation classification for reversed Dickson polynomials of the first kind
record.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $1\leq n\leq p^2-1$, and let $D_n(1,x)$ be the reversed Dickson polynomial of the first kind. A polynomial $f$ is a complete permutation polynomial (CPP) when both $f(x)$ and $f(x)+x$ permute $\mathbb{F}_p$. **Reversed Dickson complete permutation conjecture.** $D_n(1,x)$ is a CPP on $\mathbb{F}_p$ if and only if

$$
n = \begin{cases} 2,2p,3,3p,p+1,p+2,2p+1 & \text{if } p\equiv 1 \pmod{12},\\ 2,2p,3,3p & \text{if } p\equiv 3 \pmod{4}\text{ or }p\equiv 5 \pmod{12}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture is presented as strongly supported by computer searches and follows from the preceding permutation conjecture together with the results in the subsection; its general necessity remains unresolved.

record.title: Reversed Dickson second-kind permutation classification over the field of five elements
record.literal_statement:
Let $E_n(1,x)$ denote the reversed Dickson polynomial of the second kind, and let a permutation polynomial (PP) be a polynomial that permutes the field. **The $p=5$ reversed Dickson permutation conjecture.** Over $\mathbb{F}_5$, $E_n(1,x)$ is a PP if and only if

$$
n\equiv 2,3,15,94\pmod{120}.
$$

The listed residue classes are verified in the paper for the displayed representatives, but the claimed complete classification is stated as a conjecture.

record.title: The d-complete-poset LE-cactus conjecture
record.statement: Let $P$ be a d-complete poset. A poset is **LE-cactus** when its Bender–Knuth group action on its linear extensions satisfies the cactus relations. **The d-complete-poset LE-cactus conjecture.** Every d-complete poset is LE-cactus. This extends the verified result for minuscule posets and other motivating families; the general case remains open.

record.title: The concise degree-sequence graph-counting conjecture
record.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbf d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\in\mathbb N^n$ satisfy $0\le d_i\le n-1$, and let $c(\mathbf d)$ be the number of simple graphs on vertices $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ with $\deg(v_i)=d_i$ for every $i$. **Degree-sequence conciseness conjecture.** For every $k>0$, there exists $\mathbf d$ such that $c(\mathbf d)=k$ and

$$
n\le C(\log k)^c
$$

for some fixed $C,c>0$. The decision problem for graphical degree sequences is polynomial-time decidable, while the conjectured concise value realization is open and can be viewed as a binary symmetric contingency-table problem.
record.assessment: Requires every positive integer as a graph count at polynomial logarithmic vertex size. Conciseness for other counting functions is not a reduction for graphs; no gadgets with exact additive/multiplicative count control proved. Source-family earlier poset/Kronecker work distinguished.

record.title: Reversed Dickson first-kind permutation polynomial classification
record.literal_statement:
Let $p>3$ be a prime, and let $n$ satisfy $1leq nleq p^2-1$. Write $D_n(1,x)$ for the reversed Dickson polynomial of the first kind. A polynomial that permutes $\mathbb{F}_p$ is called a permutation polynomial (PP). **Reversed Dickson permutation conjecture.** $D_n(1,x)$ is a PP on $\mathbb{F}_p$ if and only if

$$
n = \begin{cases} 2,2p,3,3p,p+1,p+2,2p+1 & \text{if } p\equiv 1 \pmod{12},\\ 2,2p,3,3p,p+1 & \text{if } p\equiv 5 \pmod{12},\\ 2,2p,3,3p,p+2,2p+1 & \text{if } p\equiv 7 \pmod{12},\\ 2,2p,3,3p & \text{if } p\equiv 11 \pmod{12}.
\end{cases}
$$

The stated indices are known to be sufficient, while necessity remains open in general; the cases $p=5$ and $p=7$ are proved in the paper.

record.title: Maximum algebraic connectivity implies maximum girth
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a regular graph of degree $d$ and order $n$. Its **algebraic connectivity** is denoted by $AC(G)$, and its girth is the length of its shortest cycle.

**Maximum-connectivity–girth conjecture.** For fixed degree $d$ and order $n$, a graph maximizing $AC(G)$ also has maximum possible girth.

This conjecture is motivated by computational evidence from complete lists of cubic and quartic graphs for small orders and underlies the search for diameter-maximal graphs. It is stated as an open problem.
record.source_name: Geoffrey Exoo, Theodore Kolokolnikov, Jeanette Janssen and Timothy Salamon, “Attainable bounds for algebraic connectivity and maximally-connected regular graphs”, arXiv:2307.07308 (2023).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2201.04225](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.04225), [arXiv:1808.10203](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.10203).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07308

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2023). “We state this as an open problem.”

record.title: Monotonicity of maximum algebraic connectivity with girth
record.statement:
For integers $d$, $n$, and $g$, let $f(g;d,n)$ be the maximum possible algebraic connectivity among graphs of degree $d$, order $n$, and girth $g$.

**Algebraic-connectivity monotonicity conjecture.** The function $f(g;d,n)$ is increasing as a function of $g$.

This is presented as a stronger conjecture motivated by the same computational data on cubic and quartic graphs. It remains an open problem.

record.title: The concise symmetric Kronecker coefficient conjecture
record.statement:
For a partition $\lambda$, let $g(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ be the Kronecker coefficient and define the symmetric Kronecker coefficient by

$$
g_s(\lambda)=g(\lambda,\lambda,\lambda).
$$

A counting function is **concise** if every positive integer $k$ occurs as a value on an input whose size is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $\log k$. **Symmetric Kronecker coefficient conjecture.** The function $g_s$ is concise. The function is known to be complete and its maximum on partitions of size $n$ has exponential order, but the asserted polynomial-size realization of every value remains open.
record.source_name: Swee Hong Chan and Igor Pak, “Computational complexity of counting coincidences”, arXiv:2308.10214 (2024).

record.title: Furtula–Oz conjecture on extremal complementary second Zagreb graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, and let $cM_{2}(G)$ denote its complementary second Zagreb index, defined by

$$
cM_{2}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\left|d_{G}(u)^{2}-d_{G}(v)^{2}\right|.
$$

Here $K_m\vee\overline{K_{n-m}}$ is the join of the complete graph on $m$ vertices and the edgeless graph on $n-m$ vertices. **Furtula–Oz conjecture.** The graph with $n$ vertices and the maximum complementary second Zagreb index is isomorphic to $K_m\vee\overline{K_{n-m}}$ for some $1\leq m\leq n-1$.
This conjecture identifies the proposed extremal structure for the complementary second Zagreb index among graphs of order $n$.

record.title: The sphericity conjecture for dichotomous ordinal complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{pdd}(n)$ denote the minimum dimension required to realize a dichotomous ordinal complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathrm{sp}(G)$ be the sphericity of a graph $G$, namely the least dimension in which $G$ has a unit ball representation. Write $K_{a,b}$ for the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $a$ and $b$. **Sphericity conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{pdd}(n)=\mathrm{sp}(K_{\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil,\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor}).
$$

The complete bipartite graph is a dichotomous ordinal graph and therefore gives a lower bound for $\mathrm{pdd}(n)$. The conjecture asserts that the balanced complete bipartite graph is the most difficult such graph to realize, but the source reports no results establishing it.

record.title: The redundant-tree conjecture for highly connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $m$, and let $G$ be a $k$-connected graph. Write $\delta(G)$ for the minimum degree of $G$. A tree subgraph is **$k$-redundant** if it has the redundancy property intended in the source. **Redundant-tree conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)\geq\left\lfloor\frac{3k}{2}\right\rfloor+m-1,
$$

then $G$ contains a $k$-redundant tree isomorphic to $T$. This conjecture proposes a degree condition ensuring a prescribed redundant tree in a highly connected graph; the supplied text gives no resolution.
